hook: If your mind will not go quiet at night, do this one thing before sleep.
script: If your mind will not go quiet at night, my friend, do this one thing before you sleep, and your body will begin to change in ways you cannot imagine. Listen carefully, stay until the end, for the last part is where the peace truly lives. I am Ajahn Sutta. For fifty years I have watched the body and the mind, in silence. First, one hour before sleep, drink a small cup of warm water, not cold. Cold water wakes the fire in the belly; warm water calms it, like rain settling dust. Then lie down, and breathe the old way. The texts call it the four, seven, eight. Breathe in through the nose for four. Hold, gently, for seven. And release through the mouth for eight, long and slow, like wind leaving a valley. Do this only four times. No more. On the first breath, the heart slows. On the second, the shoulders fall. By the fourth, the mind stops chasing the day, because the body has told it, we are safe now, you may put it down. This is not medicine, my friend. It is a way. A way ten thousand monks have walked before you, on nights exactly like this one. If you will try it tonight, comment STILL below. Share it with someone whose mind never stops at night. And follow me. ...and that is enough.

pain: tired even after a full night
hook: Five signs your body never truly rests, my friend.
script: Five signs your body never truly rests, my friend. Even after a full night, you wake tired. Stay until the end, the fifth sign is the one almost everyone misses. I am Ajahn Sutta. For fifty years I have watched the body and the mind, in silence. First, you wake already braced. The jaw is tight, the hands half closed. The body slept, but it never came down from guard. Second, you sigh through the day without noticing. The breath is trying to finish something the night could not. Third, your shoulders sit up near your ears, and you only feel it when someone touches them. Fourth, by mid-morning you reach for sugar or the phone, looking for an energy that rest should have given you. And the fifth, the deepest, stillness makes you uneasy. When you finally sit with nothing to do, you feel you should be doing something. That is not rest. That is a body that forgot how. So tonight, before sleep, lie down and do only this. Soften the jaw. Drop the shoulders once, all the way. And take ten slow breaths where the out-breath is longer than the in. Ten, no more. This teaches the body it is allowed to stand down. If this found you, comment REST below. Share it with someone who wakes up tired. And follow me, my friend. ...and that is enough.

hook: When you wake at three in the morning, do this for two minutes, not your phone.
script: When you wake at three in the morning and the mind switches on, do not reach for your phone, my friend. Do this instead. It takes two minutes, and the body has a switch most people never learn. Stay until the end. I am Ajahn Sutta. For fifty years I have watched the body and the mind, in silence. When you wake in the dark, the heart is often running a little fast, and the breath is shallow and high in the chest. The mind reads this and thinks, there is danger, stay awake. So we calm the body first, and the mind will follow. Here is the way. Breathe in through the nose. Then, on top of that breath, take one more small sip of air, filling the very top of the lungs. Now let it all out through the mouth, slow and long, like wind leaving a valley. That double breath in, then the long release. Do it five times. The old ones knew this. The long out-breath tells the heart it is safe to slow. As the body settles, the thoughts lose their fuel. You are not fighting the mind. You are speaking to the body, in its own language. If you will try it tonight, comment THREE below. Share it with someone who wakes at three and cannot fall back. And follow me, my friend. ...and that is enough.

hook: The thing stealing your energy is not coffee, and it is not your age.
script: The thing stealing your energy is not coffee, my friend, and it is not your age. They told you to drink more, push harder, sleep more. But you do all of that, and still the heaviness stays. Stay until the end, for the answer is simpler than they made it. For fifty years I have watched the body, and I will tell you what the morning knows. Your body has an inner clock, older than any machine, and it waits each morning for one thing. Light. Real light, on the face, early. When the first hour passes in dim rooms and bright phones, the clock never starts, and the body spends the whole day half asleep, reaching for sugar to do what the sun should have done. So tomorrow, do this. Within the first hour of waking, go outside, even for ten minutes. No sunglasses, no screen. Let the morning light reach your eyes, even on a grey day. This single thing sets the clock, lifts the fog, and helps you sleep when night comes again. It costs nothing. It was always free. If this found you, comment LIGHT below. Share it with someone who is always tired. And follow me, my friend. ...and that is enough.

hook: Five signs your nervous system has been running too long.
script: Five signs your nervous system has been running too long, my friend. Most people carry these for years and call it normal. Stay until the end, the last one hides in plain sight. I am Ajahn Sutta, and for fifty years I have watched the body and the mind, in silence. First, you breathe high in the chest, quick and shallow, and you only notice when I mention it now. Second, you are startled easily, by a phone, a door, a voice, as if the body is always waiting for bad news. Third, your stomach is uneasy without reason, for the gut listens to the nerves more than the food. Fourth, you cannot sit without reaching for something, a screen, a snack, a task, because stillness feels unsafe. And the fifth, you are tired but wired, the body exhausted while the mind will not land. When you see these, the body is not broken. It has simply forgotten how to feel safe. So do this, three times today. Stop, and breathe out longer than you breathe in. In for four, out for eight. Three breaths. The long out-breath is the one signal the nervous system cannot ignore. If this found you, comment CALM below. Share it with someone who never relaxes. And follow me, my friend. ...and that is enough.

hook: When your heart races for no reason, breathe this way. The body has a switch.
script: When your heart begins to race for no reason, my friend, do not fight it, and do not fear it. The body has a quiet switch, and tonight I will show you where it is. Stay until the end. For fifty years I have watched the body, and I have seen this fear in ten thousand chests. A racing heart is not always danger. Often it is only a breath that has gone shallow and fast, and the heart following along. So we change the breath, and the heart obeys. Here is the way. Breathe in gently through the nose for four. Then breathe out through the mouth, slow, for six, as if cooling a bowl of soup. In for four, out for six. Do this six times. Make the out-breath the longest, softest part. The long exhale touches a nerve that runs from the chest to the deep brain, and it whispers one word the body trusts, safe. The heart hears it, and it slows. You are not powerless, my friend. You carry the switch with you, always. If this helped you, comment BREATHE below. Share it with someone whose heart races at night. And follow me. ...and that is enough.

hook: They told you to sleep eight hours. They left out the part that matters more.
script: They told you to sleep eight hours, my friend. So you lie there counting them, and still you wake unrested. Stay until the end, for they left out the part that matters more than the number. For fifty years I have watched how people sleep, and the body taught me this. The body does not love a long night. It loves a steady one. It wants to wake at the same hour each day, even the days you could sleep in. When the waking time wanders, the inner clock never settles, and even eight hours feel like four. So do this, and give it one week. Choose one waking time, and keep it every morning, weekend or not. Then, within that first hour, let morning light reach your eyes. The steady wake and the morning light are the two hands that wind the clock. Do not chase more hours, my friend. Chase the same hour. The depth you are missing lives in the rhythm, not the length. If this found you, comment RHYTHM below. Share it with someone who sleeps long and wakes tired. And follow me. ...and that is enough.

hook: Do these three things in your first five minutes awake, and the whole day changes.
script: How you wake decides how you live the day, my friend. Most people begin the morning already behind, already afraid, the thumb scrolling before the feet touch the floor. Stay until the end, and I will give you three small things for the first five minutes. For fifty years I have watched the mornings of calm people, and they share these. First, before the phone, take three slow breaths and feel the body in the bed. The phone can wait five minutes. The first thing you feed the mind should not be the world's noise. Second, drink a cup of warm water. The body has gone all night without it, and the mind clears as the body wakes. Third, let light reach your eyes, a window, a doorway, the sky. These three, breath before phone, warm water, morning light, take five minutes and ask nothing of you but the choice. Do them, and the day begins from stillness instead of fear. If you will try it tomorrow, comment MORNING below. Share it with someone whose mornings feel like a race. And follow me, my friend. ...and that is enough.

hook: The cheapest medicine for a worried mind is free, and you carry it everywhere.
script: The cheapest medicine for a worried mind is free, my friend, and you have carried it your whole life. They sell you teas and pills and apps for the thing your own breath was made to do. Stay until the end. For fifty years I have watched the breath, and I will tell you its secret. When you are anxious, the breath is fast and shallow, and this tells the brain to stay afraid. But the breath is the one part of this machine you can take into your own hands. Slow it, and the fear must follow. So do this, once a day, for five minutes. Sit. Breathe in for four. Breathe out for six. Nothing more. Let the out-breath be soft and complete, like a sigh you did not perform. Five minutes, every day, not only when the storm comes. For the breath is not only a cure for the bad moment. Practiced daily, it teaches the whole nervous system a slower way to live. It is free. It is always with you. Most people will scroll past it. If you will not, comment FREE below. Share it with someone who is always worried. And follow me, my friend. ...and that is enough.

pain: holds tension in the body all day
hook: Five places your body hides the stress you never let go of.
script: Five places your body hides the stress you never put down, my friend. You think you are relaxed, but the body keeps the score. Stay until the end, and I will give you the way to release all five in one minute. For fifty years I have watched where tension lives, and it gathers in the same five places. First, the jaw, clenched even in sleep. Second, the space between the eyebrows, drawn tight as if always solving something. Third, the shoulders, lifted toward the ears as if guarding the neck. Fourth, the hands, half closed, ready, never quite open. Fifth, the belly, held hard, never allowed to be soft. Each one is a small fist the body makes against the day. So do this now, with me. Unclench the jaw. Smooth the space between the brows. Let the shoulders fall. Open the hands, palms up. And let the belly be soft, just for one breath. That is the practice. Five soft places. Do it three times a day, at red lights, in line, before sleep, and the body learns it is allowed to put the day down. If this found you, comment SOFTEN below. Share it with someone who carries it all in their shoulders. And follow me, my friend. ...and that is enough.

hook: If you keep replaying what they did to you, here is how to set it down tonight.
script: If you keep replaying what they did to you, my friend, at red lights, in the shower, at three in the morning, listen carefully. This is not a weak mind. And tonight I will give you the exact way to set it down. Stay until the end, for the last question is the one that frees you. I am Ajahn Sutta. For fifty years I have watched the mind, in silence. First, understand this. You believe you hold the anger to protect yourself. But you are not holding it, my friend. It is holding you. Every time you replay it, they harm you again, but now you are the one pressing play. So tonight, before sleep, do this. It takes three breaths and three questions. Bring their face to mind, gently, do not run from it. Then ask, slowly. First, what were they carrying that I could not see? Second, what is this anger costing me, tonight, in my own chest, my own sleep? Third, if I set it down for just one hour, only one, what would I feel? You do not have to forgive them. That is not the task tonight. You only have to stop carrying them into your bed. Set them by the door. They will still be there in the morning, if you truly want them back. The river does not keep the leaf. It lets it pass. If you will try the three questions tonight, comment SET IT DOWN below. Share this with someone still carrying something heavy. And follow me, my friend. ...and that is enough.

hook: Five signs you are still carrying something you were meant to put down.
script: Five signs you are still carrying something you were meant to put down, my friend. You may not even know its name anymore, only its weight. Stay until the end, for the fifth is the heaviest. I am Ajahn Sutta, and for fifty years I have watched what the heart refuses to set down. First, certain songs, places, or dates make your chest tighten, and you change the subject quickly, even alone. Second, you are tired in a way sleep does not touch, the tiredness of holding. Third, you rehearse old arguments in the shower, still defending yourself to someone not there. Fourth, you keep busy on purpose, because the quiet lets the weight come close. And the fifth, you have started to believe this heaviness is simply who you are. It is not, my friend. It is only something you have carried so long the arms forgot they were holding it. So tonight, name one thing you are still carrying. Just one. Write it on paper. Then ask it a single question. Is this mine to carry, still, today? Often the honest answer is no. And in that no, the hand begins to open. If this found you, comment RELEASE below. Share it with someone who carries too much. And follow me, my friend. ...and that is enough.

hook: When your mind will not stop at night, do this. One pen, one minute.
script: When your mind will not stop at night, my friend, the same thought circling like a moth at a lamp, do not lie there fighting it. Do this. One pen, one minute. Stay until the end. For fifty years I have watched the restless mind, and I learned that the mind loops because it is afraid it will forget. It holds the thought tight, repeating, repeating, so it will not lose it before morning. So we give it somewhere safe to put it down. Keep paper beside your bed. When the looping comes, write the thought in one plain line. Then write the smallest next step beside it, the one thing you could do tomorrow. Just one line, one step. Now say to the mind, softly, it is written, you will not forget, you may rest. The mind loosens, because its job is done. The page is holding the worry now, not you. This is not avoiding the thought, my friend. It is trusting the morning to handle what the night cannot. If you will try it tonight, comment QUIET below. Share it with someone who lies awake thinking. And follow me. ...and that is enough.

hook: If you are going to replay the past, my friend, replay it differently.
script: If you are going to replay the past tonight, my friend, and you will, then at least replay it differently. Stay until the end. For fifty years I have watched the mind, and I will tell you what it does in the dark. It reaches for the worst day and plays it again, the mistake, the loss, the thing you said. The mind believes if it studies the wound enough times, it can finally fix it. But it never can, and so it plays it again. Here is the turn. You cannot stop the mind from reaching back. But you can choose what it reaches for. So tonight, when it begins, gently steer it to one good moment, and replay that with the same detail you give the pain. The light in the room. The sound of their laugh. The way the air felt. Hold it as long as the mind wants to hold the wound. You are not lying to yourself. You are simply giving the mind something true, and kinder, to chew on while you fall asleep. The past will play. Choose the scene. If this found you, comment AGAIN below. Share it with someone who relives the hard days. And follow me, my friend. ...and that is enough.

hook: You are not behind in life, my friend. Here is what is actually happening.
script: You are not behind in life, my friend. Stay with me until the end, for I want to tell you what is actually happening. You scroll, and everyone seems further along, the house, the family, the calm you cannot find. And a quiet voice says, you are late, you have wasted it. But listen. There is no single road with markers you were meant to pass by now. That was never real. It is a picture other people perform, mostly to convince themselves. The truth is, you are exactly as old as the life you have lived, no more, no less. The man who blooms late is not behind. He is blooming in his season. So tonight, do one thing. Name one true thing you did today, however small. You were patient with someone. You kept a promise to yourself. You stayed when it was hard. Name it, out loud if you can. This is not pride, my friend. It is correcting the lie that you are nothing yet. You are not behind. You are here, and here has work the future will thank you for. If this reached you, comment ENOUGH below. Share it with someone who feels too late. And follow me. ...and that is enough.

hook: How to stop the three a.m. spiral, in three breaths.
script: How to stop the three a.m. spiral, my friend, in three breaths. You know the one. You wake, and within seconds the mind has the whole future on trial, and every verdict is guilty. Stay until the end. For fifty years I have watched this hour, and I learned the first truth of it. The three a.m. mind is not telling you the truth. It is the body, low and tired, and the mind painting the dark with fear. So we do not argue with it. We do three things. First, place one hand flat on your chest, and feel it rise and fall. This brings you out of the head and into the body. Second, take three long breaths, the out-breath slow, twice as long as the in. Third, say to yourself, quietly, this is a three a.m. thought, it is not a three p.m. truth, I will look at it in the light. Then return to the breath, not the story. The spiral feeds on your attention. Give it to the breath instead, and it thins, and it fades. If you will try it tonight, comment SPIRAL below. Share it with someone who wakes in fear. And follow me, my friend. ...and that is enough.

hook: If you feel a sadness with no name, this is what it is, and the one thing to do.
script: If you feel a sadness with no name, my friend, a heaviness with nothing to point to, listen carefully. You are not broken, and you are not ungrateful. Stay until the end. For fifty years I have watched this quiet grief, and I will tell you what it often is. It is the weight of things you never let yourself feel at the time. The losses you walked past because you had to keep going. The small disappointments you told yourself did not matter. Feelings do not disappear when you ignore them. They wait. And on a quiet evening, they come together as one nameless ache. So here is the one thing to do. Do not demand a reason. Instead, place a hand over your heart, and say, simply, I feel sad, and that is allowed. Name it as sadness, not as failure. Let it be there, like weather, without fixing it. Often the ache only wanted to be felt, not solved. When you stop fighting it, it begins to soften, the way a child stops crying once it is finally held. If this reached you, comment NAME below. Share it with someone carrying a quiet weight. And follow me, my friend. ...and that is enough.

pain: at war with your own mind
hook: You do not need to quiet your mind, my friend. You need to stop believing it.
script: You do not need to quiet your mind, my friend. You have tried for years, and it will not obey. Stay until the end, for the freedom is not where you have been looking. For fifty years I have watched the mind, and here is what I learned. The mind makes thoughts the way the eye makes seeing. You cannot stop it, and you do not need to. The suffering is not the thought. The suffering is believing every thought is true, and every thought is you. But watch closely tonight. A harsh thought comes, you are not enough. Instead of fighting it, ask one question. Would I say this to a friend I love? If the answer is no, then it is not wisdom speaking. It is only an old habit, wearing your voice. You do not have to silence it. You only have to stop bowing to it. Let the thought pass through, the way a cloud passes the moon without staining it. You are not the cloud, my friend. You are the sky it moves across. If this found you, comment WATCH below. Share it with someone at war with their own mind. And follow me. ...and that is enough.

hook: The two-minute practice that ends overthinking before sleep.
script: The mind will not stop at night. You lie down, and it begins, every conversation, every worry, again and again. Tonight I will give you a two-minute practice that ends it, my friend. Stay until the end, for the last part is the key. I am Ajahn Sutta. For fifty years I have watched the mind, in silence. Here is the truth. You cannot stop a thought by pushing it away. Push it, and it pushes back. So we do not fight. We name. As you lie in the dark, when a thought comes, say one word in your mind, softly. Thinking. That is all. A worry about tomorrow arrives, thinking. The memory you hate, thinking. You are not judging it, not following it. You are naming it, the way you would name a bird that lands and flies off. Each time you name it, you step back one pace, and the thought loosens its grip. Do this, and you will notice something. You are not your thoughts. You are the one who notices them. And that one is already calm. It was always calm. If you will try it tonight, comment LABEL below. Share it with someone whose mind never stops. And follow me, my friend. ...and that is enough.

hook: They told you to forgive to find peace. There is an easier first step.
script: They told you that to find peace, you must forgive the one who hurt you. And you have tried, my friend, and it would not come. So you decided peace was not for you. Listen carefully. There is an easier first step, and it is not forgiveness. Stay until the end. I am Ajahn Sutta. For fifty years I have watched the mind, in silence. Forgiveness is a door at the end of a long road. But you do not have to reach that door tonight. Tonight you only have to stop carrying them to bed. There is a difference between holding someone accountable and holding them in your chest at two in the morning. The first is justice. The second only harms you. So do this. When their face comes to mind tonight, do not push it away, and do not forgive it. Simply say, I am setting you by the door. You will still be there in the morning, if I truly want to pick you up again. And then turn toward sleep. You are not letting them win. You are letting yourself rest. Forgiveness, if it ever comes, will come later, on its own. If this reached you, comment PEACE below. Share it with someone carrying an old wound. And follow me, my friend. ...and that is enough.

hook: Five signs your body is quietly thirsty, and it is aging you faster than you know.
script: Five signs your body is quietly thirsty, my friend, and it is aging you faster than you know. Stay until the end, the fourth surprises everyone. For fifty years I have watched the body, and water is the first medicine. First, you wake with a dry mouth and a dull head, the night spent without a drop. Second, your skin is slow to settle when you pinch it gently on the back of the hand. Third, you feel hungry soon after eating, for the body confuses thirst for hunger. Fourth, your afternoon tiredness arrives like clockwork, and you reach for coffee when water would serve you better. Fifth, your thoughts grow foggy by evening, for even the mind runs on water. So do this. Each morning, before the coffee, drink one full cup of warm water, slowly. And keep water near you through the day, sipping, not flooding. This one habit clears the head, softens the skin, and steadies the energy. The body is mostly water, my friend. Treat it like a well, not a desert. If this found you, comment WATER below. Share it with someone always tired in the afternoon. And follow me. ...and that is enough.

hook: If you cannot fall asleep, the problem begins one hour before bed, not in the bed.
script: If you cannot fall asleep, my friend, the problem often begins one hour before you lie down, not in the bed itself. Stay until the end. For fifty years I have watched how people end their day, and the body needs a signal that night has come. We live in bright rooms until the moment we close our eyes, and the body never learns it is time. So give it the signal. One hour before sleep, do three things. First, lower the lights, lamps not ceiling lights, dim and warm like a small fire. Second, put the bright screen away, or make it as dim and warm as it will go. Third, drink a small cup of warm water and let the body slow. Bright light tells the brain it is still day, and it holds back the rest that sleep is made of. Lower the light, and the body remembers the old rhythm of the sun. Do this for one week. You are not forcing sleep, my friend. You are telling the body the truth, that night has come, and it is safe to rest. If this helped you, comment DUSK below. Share it with someone who lies awake. And follow me. ...and that is enough.

hook: The reason you crave sugar at night is not weakness, and it is not hunger.
script: The reason you crave sugar at night is not weakness, my friend, and it is not hunger. Stay until the end, for once you see it, the craving loosens its grip. For fifty years I have watched the body, and the evening sweet tooth tells an old story. By night, you are often not hungry at all. You are tired, or unsettled, or simply seeking a small comfort after a long day. The body learned that sugar brings a quick warmth, a brief peace, so it asks, again and again. But the peace fades fast, and the asking returns. So next time the craving comes, before you answer it, do this. Drink a glass of water, and take ten slow breaths, the out-breath long. Then wait, just five minutes. Often you will find the craving was never about food. It was the body asking to be soothed, and the breath soothed it instead. You are not weak, my friend. You were answering the wrong question. If this found you, comment SWEET below. Share it with someone who battles the night cravings. And follow me. ...and that is enough.

hook: If your neck and shoulders turn to stone by evening, do this. Sixty seconds.
script: If your shoulders and neck turn to stone by evening, my friend, this is for you, and it takes sixty seconds. Stay until the end. For fifty years I have watched where the day collects in the body, and it gathers in the neck and shoulders, the place we brace when we are braced against life. So we release it, gently, now. First, lift both shoulders up toward your ears, tight, hold for one breath, then let them drop all at once, fully. Do this three times. Second, slowly lower one ear toward one shoulder, feel the long side of the neck open, breathe, then the other side. Third, unclench the jaw, for the jaw and the neck hold hands, and one will not soften while the other stays hard. Sixty seconds, three times a day. You will not undo a lifetime of tension in a minute, my friend. But you will remind the body, again and again, that it is allowed to set the weight down. If this helped you, comment EASE below. Share it with someone who carries the day in their neck. And follow me. ...and that is enough.

pain: stress shows up as gut trouble
hook: Five signs your gut is not sick, my friend. It is stressed.
script: Five signs your gut is not sick, my friend. It is stressed. Stay until the end, for the fifth is the one rarely mentioned. For fifty years I have watched the body, and the belly is where the nerves keep their secrets. First, your stomach knots before a hard conversation, long before any food is involved. Second, your digestion changes when your life does, in grief, in worry, in change. Third, you feel butterflies, or a sinking, in the gut and not the head. Fourth, eating in a rush leaves you heavy and uneasy, the body too tense to receive the food. Fifth, calm days digest easily, and anxious days do not. The gut listens to the mind more than to the meal. So do this before you eat. Take three slow breaths, let the shoulders fall, and eat the first few bites slowly, with attention. A calm body digests. A braced body cannot. You may not need a new diet, my friend. You may need a calmer table. If this found you, comment BELLY below. Share it with someone whose stomach carries their stress. And follow me. ...and that is enough.

hook: They told you to just think positive, my friend. There is a kinder, truer first step.
script: They told you to just think positive, my friend. And you tried, and it felt like lying to yourself. Stay until the end, for there is a kinder, truer first step. For fifty years I have watched the mind, and forced positivity is thin paint over a deep crack. The feeling underneath does not leave because you smiled at it. It only waits, and grows. So before the positive, do the honest. When something hurts, name it plainly, first. Say, this is hard. Or, I feel afraid. Or, I am sad. Let it be true for one moment, without rushing to fix it. This is not negativity, my friend. It is honesty, and honesty is where real peace begins. Only after the feeling is seen can a kinder thought take root, and then it is not a lie, it is a choice. Do not paint over the crack. See it first. The seeing is what heals. If this reached you, comment HONEST below. Share it with someone tired of pretending to be fine. And follow me, my friend. ...and that is enough.

hook: There is a one-line practice that changes the mind, but most people do it wrong.
script: There is a one-line practice, my friend, that slowly changes the mind, but only if you do it correctly, for most people do it wrong. Stay until the end. For fifty years I have watched the mind, and it leans toward what is missing, what went wrong, what is feared. This was useful long ago, when danger was everywhere. But now it steals your peace. So each night, write down one good thing from the day. Not a list. Just one. But here is the part most people miss. Do not write the thing alone. Write why it mattered to you. Not, a good meal, but, a good meal, because I ate it slowly and felt at peace for once. The why is what teaches the mind to look for the good, not merely to list it. One specific thing, and its why, each night. Slowly, the mind learns a new lean. You are not forcing happiness, my friend. You are training attention, the way you would train a young dog, gently, daily. If you will try it tonight, comment ONE below. Share it with someone whose mind dwells on the hard. And follow me. ...and that is enough.

hook: If you do not feel sad, my friend, but numb, as if behind glass, listen carefully.
script: If you do not feel sad, my friend, but numb, as if you are watching life from behind glass, listen carefully. This is not coldness, and you are not broken. Stay until the end. For fifty years I have watched the mind, and numbness is often the heart's own mercy. When feeling becomes too much, for too long, the mind turns the sound down, to protect you. It was a kindness, once. But left too long, the glass keeps out the joy along with the pain. So we begin gently, through the body, not the mind. Today, do one small thing with full attention.
